short_bio_en: A man of Zheng who wrote his own penal code on bamboo strips, a generation after Zichan had cast the state's code in bronze. In 501 BCE the Zheng government killed him and then adopted his code. The chronicle's own verdict is that this was disloyal: if you use a man's way, you should not throw the man away.

name_alt: Wei Si; 斯 (the personal name in Shiji 15); 都 (the personal name in Shiji 44)
role_tag_en: first ruler of Wei to be ranked a marquis; patron of reformers
dating_basis: Reign and death from Shiji 15 六國年表, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): the 魏 column reads 魏文侯斯元年 at the line the edition labels 424, runs his years to 三十八 at the line labelled 387, and reads 魏武侯元年 at 386. Shiji 44 魏世家, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷044 (revision 7903606, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session), agrees on the length: 卅八年 ... 是歳，文侯卒，子撃立，是爲武侯. The western years are the edition's leftmost column (each linked to a w:前N年 article), the edition's own conversion and not Sima Qian's (calendars.csv CAL_ZHOU_REGNAL). The two chapters disagree on his personal name: the table writes 斯, Shiji 44 writes 桓子之孫曰文侯都; both are carried in name_alt and neither is chosen. No birth year is given; blank. Other chronologies for this reign exist outside the Shiji; none was read this session and none is asserted. Reign -424/-387 straddles the 600-400 slice's lower boundary.
short_bio_en: Ruler of Wei, one of the three houses that divided the old state of Jin, and in 403 BCE among the first of them to be ranked a marquis. The Shiji pictures his court as the first to collect scholars and reformers deliberately: he took instruction from Confucius's disciple Zixia, put Ximen Bao in charge of Ye, asked Li Ke whom to make chief minister, and is credited with sponsoring Li Kui's agrarian policy.

role_tag_en: Wei minister credited with state farm policy and an early law code
dating_basis: No birth or death year is given by any source read; both ranges blank. Active under Marquis Wen of Wei (reign -424/-387, P_MARQUIS_WEN_WEI): 漢書 卷二十四 食貨志, read at zh.wikisource.org page 漢書/卷024 (revision 7498330, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session), 李悝為魏文侯作盡地力之教; Shiji 74, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷074 (revision 7908177, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session), 魏有李悝，盡地力之教. THE WITNESSES ARE LATE AND THIN: Sima Qian (c. -100) gives one clause; Ban Gu's Hanshu (1st century CE) gives the policy's arithmetic; the title 法經 is attested only in the 晉書 刑法志, read at zh.wikisource.org page 晉書/卷030 (revision 2687304, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session), a Tang-dynasty compilation (the page header names 房玄齡; the page's own licence notice calls it 此唐朝作品), more than a thousand years after Marquis Wen (E_CN_046). The Han catalogue lists 李子三十二篇 under 法家 (漢書 卷三十, read at zh.wikisource.org page 漢書/卷030 (revision 7908197, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session)); the book is lost. CONTESTED IDENTITY, STATED AND NOT RESOLVED: Shiji 15 (the 魏 column at the line labelled 405, 卜相，李克、翟璜爭) and Shiji 44 (魏文侯謂李克曰...) name a minister 李克 at the same court; whether 李悝 and 李克 are one man is a scholarly question no source read this session settles. This row is 李悝, the name the policy and the code are attached to; 李克 is carried in name_alt as a contested identification, and no event or relation here rests on the identification.
short_bio_en: Minister of Marquis Wen of Wei around 400 BCE, remembered for two things. Han historians credit him with a farm policy that calculated how much grain a state could gain from diligent cultivation and with a state granary that bought cheap and sold dear to keep prices stable. A much later history makes him the compiler of the first code of laws, which it says the Qin reformer Shang Yang took with him to Qin. Whether he is the same man as the minister Li Ke is disputed.

name_alt: Wei Yang; 衛鞅; Gongsun Yang; 公孫鞅; Lord of Shang; 商君
role_tag_en: Qin minister whose reforms built the centralised state
dating_basis: Death: Shiji 15 六國年表, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): the 秦 column at the line the edition labels 338 reads 二十四。（秦）大荔圍合陽。孝公薨。商君反，死彤地。 and the 魏 column of the same line 三十三。衛鞅亡歸我，我恐，弗內。 Shiji 5 秦本紀, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷005 (revision 8744286, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session), puts it in the year Duke Xiao died: 孝公卒，子惠文君立。是歲，誅衛鞅。 Shiji 68 商君列傳, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷068 (revision 8764712, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session), tells it at length and names a different place: 秦發兵攻商君，殺之於鄭黽池。秦惠王車裂商君以徇，曰：「莫如商鞅反者！」遂滅商君之家。 The two places (彤地 in the table, 鄭黽池 in the biography) are both carried and neither is chosen (E_CN_054). Active from his arrival in Qin in Duke Xiao's first year (Shiji 5: 衛鞅聞是令下，西入秦，因景監求見孝公。; 秦孝公元年 at the line labelled 361 in Shiji 15) to his death. No birth year is given; blank. The western years are the edition's leftmost column (each cell links a w:前N年 article), the edition's own conversion and not Sima Qian's (calendars.csv CAL_ZHOU_REGNAL). Range wholly after the 600-400 BCE pilot slice; admitted for the China pillar by D-20 (R_CN ranges over 800-200). polity_id is BLANK: he served Qin, and this dataset has no Qin polity row; a Qin row needs both ends of its range read at a locator, which this batch did not do (raised in CHANGES.md, the POL_SONG precedent).
short_bio_en: A noble of the small state of Wey (衛) who went west to Qin in 361 BCE and persuaded Duke Xiao to remake it: households grouped in fives and tens and made answerable for one another's crimes, rank given for enemy heads taken in battle, villages merged into counties under appointed magistrates, and one standard for weights and measures. Qin's later conquest of all the states ran on this machinery. When the duke died, the members of the ruling house he had offended accused him of rebellion; he was killed and his body torn apart by chariots. The book that bears his name was put together by his followers.

role_tag_en: Han chancellor who made the control of officials an art
dating_basis: Office and death: Shiji 15 六國年表, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): the 韓 column at the line labelled 351 reads 八。申不害相。 and at 337 二十二。申不害卒。 Shiji 63, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷063 (revision 7903601, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 申不害者，京人也，故鄭之賤臣。學術以干韓昭侯，昭侯用為相。內修政教，外應諸侯，十五年。終申子之身，國治兵彊，無侵韓者。申子之學本於黃老而主刑名。著書二篇，號曰申子。 The Shiji's fifteen years match the table's lines -351 to -337 counted inclusively. Han Feizi 定法, read at zh.wikisource.org page 韓非子/定法 (revision 2327670, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session), gives seventeen (故託万乘之勁韓，十七年而不至於霸王者); both counts are carried and the table's years are used. No birth year is given; blank. HIS TEXT: the Shiji's 申子 in two pian and the Han catalogue's 申子六篇 (Hanshu 30, SRC_WS_HANSHU_30) are lost. The wikisource page 申子 (revision 7532852, read this session) is an unattributed modern assembly of fragments with no edition statement and no licence notice in either form; it is NOT used as an edition (L-105(7)). His words in this dataset are cited only from a carrier text: Q_123, Han Feizi 定法, 申子言：『治不踰官，雖知弗言。』 The western years are the edition's leftmost column (each cell links a w:前N年 article), the edition's own conversion and not Sima Qian's (calendars.csv CAL_ZHOU_REGNAL). Range wholly after the 600-400 BCE pilot slice; admitted for the China pillar by D-20 (R_CN ranges over 800-200).
short_bio_en: A minor official from the old state of Zheng who became chancellor of Han in 351 BCE and held the post until his death fifteen years later. Where Shang Yang trusted written law, Shen Buhai taught the ruler technique (術): appoint men to posts, hold each to the exact duties of his title, and judge him by results. His own book is lost; what survives of his words is quoted by others, above all by Han Fei.

role_tag_en: general and reformer who served Lu, Wei and Chu
dating_basis: Shiji 65 孫子吳起列傳, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷065 (revision 2567048, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session), is the only biography. Death: 及悼王死，宗室大臣作亂而攻吳起，吳起走之王尸而伏之。擊起之徒因射刺吳起，并中悼王。悼王既葬，太子立，乃使令尹盡誅射吳起而并中王尸者。坐射起而夷宗死者七十餘家。 Shiji 15 六國年表, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): the 楚 column reads 楚悼王類元年 at the line labelled 401 and 楚肅王臧元年 at 380, so King Dao's last year is the line labelled 381; Wu Qi was killed when the king died and his killers punished after the burial under the new king, hence -381/-380. Career: Lu (吳起者，衛人也，好用兵。嘗學於曾子，事魯君。); Wei under Marquis Wen and his son (於是魏文侯以為將，擊秦，拔五城。 … 文侯以吳起善用兵，廉平，盡能得士心，乃以為西河守，以拒秦、韓。魏文侯既卒，起事其子武侯。); then Chu (吳起懼得罪，遂去，即之楚。). Han Feizi 和氏, read at zh.wikisource.org page 韓非子/和氏 (revision 2327657, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session), has the Chu reform last a year: 悼王行之期年而薨矣，吴起枝解於楚 (Q_127). LINEAGE: 遂事曾子。居頃之，其母死，起終不歸。曾子薄之，而與起絕。 (LIN_022, reliability low). No birth year is given; blank. polity_id is blank: he served three states (Lu, Wei, Chu) and one FK cannot carry them. The western years are the edition's leftmost column (each cell links a w:前N年 article), the edition's own conversion and not Sima Qian's (calendars.csv CAL_ZHOU_REGNAL). Range wholly after the 600-400 BCE pilot slice; admitted for the China pillar by D-20 (R_CN ranges over 800-200).
short_bio_en: A soldier from Wey (衛) who served three states. In Wei he commanded against Qin for Marquis Wen and governed the western frontier; in Chu, as chief minister to King Dao, he abolished offices the state did not need, stripped royal kinsmen of distant descent of their privileges and spent the savings on the army. When the king died the nobles attacked him; he threw himself on the king's body, the arrows that killed him struck the corpse too, and the new king put more than seventy families to death for it. Han Fei paired him with Shang Yang as the reformer the old nobility destroys.

name_alt: Xun Qing; 荀卿; Sun Qing; 孫卿; Xun Kuang
role_tag_en: Ru thinker who held human nature bad and ritual its cure
dating_basis: CONTESTED DATING, WIDE RANGE, LOW RELIABILITY (the task book's terms). Birth and death are BLANK because the sources read cannot fix either. Shiji 74, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷074 (revision 7908177, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 荀卿，趙人。年五十始來游學於齊。 田駢之屬皆已死齊襄王時，而荀卿最為老師。齊尚修列大夫之缺，而荀卿三為祭酒焉。齊人或讒荀卿，荀卿乃適楚，而春申君以為蘭陵令。春申君死而荀卿廢，因家蘭陵。李斯嘗為弟子，已而相秦。 … 於是推儒、墨、道德之行事興壞，序列著數萬言而卒。因葬蘭陵。 Shiji 15 六國年表, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 齊宣王辟彊元年 at the line labelled 342, 齊湣王地元年 at 323, 齊襄王法章元年 at 283; 楚考烈王元年。秦取我州。黃歇為相。 at 262; and 二十五。李園殺春申君。 at 238 (the 楚 column: from the line labelled 246 the first cell spans the 周 and 秦 columns, so the cell is identified by its reign count, Kaolie 25). THE CONTRADICTION, IN THE WORK'S OWN INDEX NOTE (荀子, revision 1641418; the note is in the form of a Siku catalogue entry and the page does not name its source, so it is cited as the page's note): 考劉向《序錄》，卿以齊宣王時來游稷下，後仕楚，春申君死而卿廢。然《[[史記]]‧六國年表》載春申君之死，上距宣王之末凡八十七年。《史記》稱卿年五十始游齊，則春申君死之年，卿年當一百三十七矣，於理不近。 … 總之戰國時人爾，其生卒年月已不可確考矣。 That is: on Liu Xiang's account (as the note quotes it) he came to Qi under King Xuan (-342/-324), aged fifty by the Shiji, which would make him about 137 when the Lord of Chunshen was killed in -238; the note reports Chao Gongwu's emendation of 'fifty' to 'fifteen' as possible, and Song Lian's placing of the visit under King Xiang as unsupported. The floruit is carried as one activity event, -342/-238, reliability low (E_CN_058); no birth or death range is asserted. polity_id is blank: a man of Zhao (趙人) who served Qi's academy and Chu's Lanling. The western years are the edition's leftmost column (each cell links a w:前N年 article), the edition's own conversion and not Sima Qian's (calendars.csv CAL_ZHOU_REGNAL). Range wholly after the 600-400 BCE pilot slice; admitted for the China pillar by D-20 (R_CN ranges over 800-200).
short_bio_en: A scholar from Zhao who became the senior teacher at the court academy of Qi and later magistrate of Lanling in Chu, where he died. Against Mencius he argued that human nature is bad and that goodness is made, by teachers, ritual and law, as a craftsman straightens warped wood. Two of his students, Han Fei and Li Si, became the theorist and the minister of Qin's unification. His dates cannot be fixed: the early accounts of his life contradict one another by decades.

name_alt: Hanfeizi; 韓非子; Hanzi; 韓子
role_tag_en: Han prince who joined law, technique and power into one theory
dating_basis: Death: Shiji 6 秦始皇本紀, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷006 (revision 7907969, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 十四年，攻趙軍於平陽，取宜安，破之，殺其將軍。桓齮定平陽、武城。韓非使秦，秦用李斯謀，留非，非死雲陽。韓王請為臣。 The First Emperor's first year is the line labelled 246 in Shiji 15 六國年表, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session) (始皇帝元年。擊取晉陽，作鄭國渠。), so his 14th year is -233. Shiji 63, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷063 (revision 7903601, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 韓非者，韓之諸公子也。喜刑名法術之學，而其歸本於黃老。 … 與李斯俱事荀卿，斯自以為不如非。 … 李斯使人遺非藥，使自殺。韓非欲自陳，不得見。秦王後悔之，使人赦之，非已死矣。 No birth year is given; blank. The western years are the edition's leftmost column (each cell links a w:前N年 article), the edition's own conversion and not Sima Qian's (calendars.csv CAL_ZHOU_REGNAL). Range wholly after the 600-400 BCE pilot slice; admitted for the China pillar by D-20 (R_CN ranges over 800-200).
short_bio_en: A prince of the weak state of Han who stammered and could not argue aloud but wrote with great force. He studied with Xunzi alongside Li Si, and drew the strands of earlier statecraft together: Shang Yang's published law, Shen Buhai's technique for controlling officials, and the power of the ruler's position. The king of Qin read two of his essays and wanted to meet him; when Han Fei came to Qin as an envoy in 233 BCE, Li Si had him handed to the officials and sent him poison.

role_tag_en: Xunzi's student who became chancellor of Qin's empire
dating_basis: Shiji 87 李斯列傳, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷087 (revision 2364605, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 李斯者，楚上蔡人也。 … 乃從荀卿學帝王之術。 … 官至廷尉。二十餘年，竟并天下，尊主為皇帝，以斯為丞相。 … 二世二年七月，具斯五刑，論腰斬咸陽市。 Shiji 15 六國年表, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): the line labelled 208, a single cell spanning the table, reads 二將軍章邯、長史司馬欣、都尉董翳追楚兵至河。誅丞相斯、去疾，將軍馮劫。 (the Second Emperor's year 2: 二世元年 heads the line labelled 209). No birth year is given; blank. polity_id is blank: he served Qin (no Qin polity row; raised in CHANGES.md). Added as an index row because the sources read tie him to three rows of this batch: Xunzi's pupil (Shiji 74, Shiji 87; LIN_021), the instigator of Han Fei's death (Shiji 63, Shiji 6; E_CN_059), and the minister whose argument set up the commanderies in 221 (Shiji 6; E_CN_060). The western years are the edition's leftmost column (each cell links a w:前N年 article), the edition's own conversion and not Sima Qian's (calendars.csv CAL_ZHOU_REGNAL). Range wholly after the 600-400 BCE pilot slice; admitted for the China pillar by D-20 (R_CN ranges over 800-200).
short_bio_en: A clerk from Shangcai in Chu who studied statecraft with Xunzi and went to Qin as the other states were being swallowed. In 221 BCE, as commandant of justice, he argued against making the emperor's sons kings of the conquered lands, and the empire was divided instead into commanderies under appointed governors; he became chancellor. The Shiji also makes him responsible for the death of his fellow student Han Fei. Under the Second Emperor he was accused of treason and cut in two in the market at Xianyang in 208 BCE.

role_tag_en: persuader credited with the alliance against Qin; record contested
dating_basis: CONTESTED, with P_ZHANGYI (the two enter together or not at all: task book). Shiji 15 六國年表, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): the 燕 column at the line labelled 334 reads 二十八。蘇秦說燕。 (燕文公元年 at 361). Shiji 69 蘇秦列傳, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷069 (revision 2621145, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 蘇秦者，東周雒陽人也。東事師於齊，而習之於鬼谷先生。 … 去游燕，歲餘而後得見。說燕文侯曰 … 於是六國從合而并力焉。蘇秦為從約長，并相六國。 DEATH, FROM THE CHAPTER'S NARRATIVE ORDER, NOT FROM A DATED LINE: he is killed in Qi after Yan's King Kuai succeeds (燕易王卒，燕噲立為王。其後齊大夫多與蘇秦爭寵者，而使人刺蘇秦; 燕王噲元年 at 320 in Shiji 15), and the chapter tells the Zizhi affair after his death (燕相子之與蘇代婚 …; Shiji 15, 七。君噲及太子相子之皆死。 at 314): -320/-314. WHY CONTESTED: Sima Qian warns against his own material in the chapter's closing judgement: 然世言蘇秦多異，異時事有類之者皆附之蘇秦。 — stories of other men and other times were attached to Su Qin's name. The Mawangdui silk letters, presented on wikisource as 戰國縱橫家書 (page header title 漢代縱橫家書, revision 2630094, read this session), are commonly set against the Shiji's chronology, but that page names no author and no edition for its modern transcription and renders no licence notice in either form; its licence is unconfirmed, it was NOT used, and no argument in this dataset rests on it (L-105(7)). historicity 'probable' for the Shiji's own caution. The western years are the edition's leftmost column (each cell links a w:前N年 article), the edition's own conversion and not Sima Qian's (calendars.csv CAL_ZHOU_REGNAL). Range wholly after the 600-400 BCE pilot slice; admitted for the China pillar by D-20 (R_CN ranges over 800-200).
short_bio_en: A man of Luoyang remembered as the strategist of the 'vertical' alliance (合從): the states east of Qin binding together against the strongest power. The Shiji has him persuade the rulers one by one, carry the seals of six states at once, and die murdered in Qi. Sima Qian himself warned that many stories told of Su Qin belonged to other men and other times, and the chronology of his career is disputed.

role_tag_en: Qin chancellor who broke alliances by separate bargains
dating_basis: Offices and death: Shiji 15 六國年表, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): the 秦 column reads 十。張儀相。 at the line labelled 328, 三。張儀免相，相魏。 at 322 and 八。…張儀復相。 at 317; the 楚 column 十六。張儀來相。 at 313; the 秦 column 秦武王元年。…張儀、魏章皆出之魏。 at 310; and the 魏 column 十。張儀死。 at 309. Shiji 70 張儀列傳, read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷070 (revision 2621148, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 張儀者，魏人也。始嘗與蘇秦俱事鬼谷先生，學術，蘇秦自以不及張儀。 … 惠王乃以張儀為相，更名少梁曰夏陽。 … 張儀相魏一歲，卒於魏也。 CONTESTED PAIRING (with P_SUQIN): the chapter's closing judgement treats the two together (夫張儀之行事甚於蘇秦，然世惡蘇秦者，以其先死，而儀振暴其短以扶其說，成其衡道。要之，此兩人真傾危之士哉！), and its narrative of Su Qin sending Zhang Yi to Qin depends on Su Qin's disputed chronology. The Qin table records Zhang Yi's offices independently of that story, so his historicity is 'attested'; the pairing is what is contested (REL_036). No birth year is given; blank. polity_id blank: he served Qin, Wei and Chu. The western years are the edition's leftmost column (each cell links a w:前N年 article), the edition's own conversion and not Sima Qian's (calendars.csv CAL_ZHOU_REGNAL). Range wholly after the 600-400 BCE pilot slice; admitted for the China pillar by D-20 (R_CN ranges over 800-200).
short_bio_en: A man of Wei who, as chancellor of Qin from 328 BCE, worked the opposite strategy to Su Qin's: the 'horizontal' policy (衡), detaching states from any alliance against Qin by separate bargains with each. He moved between the chancellorships of Qin, Wei and Chu and died in Wei in 309 BCE. The Shiji makes him Su Qin's fellow student and rival, a pairing that rests partly on Su Qin's disputed story.
